We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 step (i.e., one reaction) from commercially available precursors, total price <= $250. The earlier template 1229769 gave precursors: C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCCC1=O and C[Si](C)(C)C(F)(F)F. The second is a silyl trifluoromethyl reagent (trimethylsilyl trifluoromethyl?). That is likely not commercially available or expensive. Also verification step failed (maybe because template not appropriate). Need find a different disconnection.

The target: an alkene attached to aromatic phenyl (styrene-like) and a cyclopentane with OH and CF3 attached to same carbon (a tertiary carbon bearing OH and CF3). The structure: (E?) CH2= C(aryl) - chiral carbon attached to cyclopentane ring with OH and CF3.

Potential retrosynthesis: disconnection of CF3 introduction via electrophilic trifluoromethylation of a tertiary alcohol? Or start from a ketone then reduce? Could consider using a gem-difluoro? Actually CF3 attached to carbon bearing OH (i.e., tertiary alcohol with CF3). Could be formed by addition of CF3- to a carbonyl (e.g., trifluoromethylation of a ketone to give tertiary alcohol). So precursor could be the same skeleton but carbonyl instead of CF3 and OH: i.e., a ketone (C=O) at that carbon, then nucleophilic addition of CF3- (e.g., Ruppert-Prakash reagent TMS-CF3) to give CF3-bearing alcohol. So precursor: same molecule but carbonyl instead of CF3 and OH? Actually target has CF3 and OH on same carbon (C bearing OH and CF3). Starting from ketone (C=O) at that carbon, then addition of CF3- gives CF3-CH(OH). But need also the OH present; addition of CF3- to ketone yields tertiary alcohol with CF3 and OH? Yes, CF3- adds to carbonyl, giving alkoxide then protonation yields CF3-CH(OH). So precursor: same skeleton but carbonyl (C=O) instead of CF3 and OH? Actually the carbon currently is attached to OH and CF3 and also attached to cyclopentane chain and the alkene side. In ketone precursor, it would be carbonyl attached to cyclopentane chain and alkene side, no OH, no CF3. So precursor SMILES: [CH2]=[C]([c1ccccc1])[C@@H]1CCCC1=O (i.e., the same as earlier C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCCC1=O). That is the same as the first precursor from template 1229769. So we could use that ketone as precursor, then do trifluoromethylation (CF3 addition) using TMS-CF3 (trimethyl(trifluoromethyl)silane) as reagent. That reagent is commercially available (maybe expensive). Need price check.

Search for TMS-CF3 (SMILES C[Si](C)(C)C(F)(F)F). Already earlier we saw it's buyable (True). Need price. Use search_catalog_by_smiles for that reagent.
